snapshot_note: v0.54.0 released on develop 2026-07-27 — six C++ correctness fixes, four of them SILENT wrong answers, all found by following one reducer down. A qualified name in an OPERAND position was returned bare instead of continuing its postfix chain, so every ( [ . -> after it was dropped and re-read by the caller as a fresh expression: (int)N::f(x) silently became (int)(x) and --emit=c11 printed `return "abc";`, while (int)N::arr[1] sent the orphaned [ to the LAMBDA-introducer dispatch. Under that sat (int)S::f(4) reporting "undeclared identifier 'S'" — the shape every string header is built from — where the operand path carried a narrow COPY of the class-qualifier rule that the shared resolver (four other callers) already owned. Under THAT, a static data member read as 0 from inside its own class body where g++ gives 42: storage was registered only by the out-of-class definition, which is parsed after member-function bodies. g++'s model transferred exactly (finish_static_data_member_decl creates the decl in the class body; the definition COMPLETES that decl) and madc's DECL_IN_AGGR_P turned out to be vfEXTERN, whose completion addVariable already implemented — nothing new was invented. Also: a nested type is now a member of its enclosing scope with `struct` spelled too, earning class-hood alongside an object member and an NSDMI on the principle the promotion site already stated (the keyword does not decide struct-vs-class, the contents do). TWO OF THREE BATTERIES ON THE STATIC-MEMBER FIX WENT RED and 45 green reducers said nothing about either — the suite found what the reducers structurally could not. Shipped with two labelled placeholders: system-header class statics still fold (no Itanium storage_alias_name for class statics yet — itanium_mangle_nested_var already takes an arbitrary qualifier chain, so it is within reach), and two scopes each declaring `struct Inner` still collide. Fork unchanged (1.0-madc.0.52.0 @ba216dea).

⚠⚠ THREE BATTERIES, TWO OF THEM RED, AND THE REDUCERS COULD NOT HAVE CAUGHT EITHER. The static-member fix broke 4 UNIT tests, then (after the first guard) 4 INTEGRATION tests. Both failures were the same shape — the CIR emitting references to static-member storage symbols that nothing in the TU defines — but a DIFFERENT class of symbol each time, and 45 green reducers said nothing, because a user class's static always has its definition in the same file. THE SUITE FOUND WHAT THE REDUCERS STRUCTURALLY COULD NOT. I also BISECTED (built state D alone) instead of guessing which of the two changes did it.

FIX 1 @cff57761 — a static data member's DECLARATION introduces its storage. `struct C { static int n; static int get(void){ return n; } }; int C::n = 42;` gave 0 for g++'s 42, SILENT, exit 0; writes said "lvalue required". Storage was registered only by the out-of-class definition, parsed AFTER member-function bodies. g++ does the reverse (finish_static_data_member_decl, gcc/cp/decl2.cc:1167): the decl is created while parsing the CLASS BODY and the definition COMPLETES THAT SAME DECL. madc's DECL_IN_AGGR_P is vfEXTERN and addVariable's existing-symbol branch ALREADY implemented the completion (adopt type/count, clear flag, same Variable) — nothing new was invented.
  GUARD 1 (correct, keep): only a member with NO in-class initializer. g++'s own DECL_INITIAL distinction. basic_string<...>::npos and memory_resource::_S_max_align carry initializers madc cannot capture as integers and have no definition here.
  GUARD 2 (PLACEHOLDER — DELETE IT, do not read it as a design decision): skip classes from SYSTEM HEADERS. locale::_S_once / locale::id::_S_refcount / ios_base::Init::_S_synced_with_stdio have no initializer AND no definition in the TU (they are in libstdc++.so).

⚠ OWNER SAW THE REAL ANSWER AND I HAD OVERSTATED THE COST: "don't we just need to add libc++ style mangling support?" — essentially YES, and it is not libc++-specific (libstdc++ and libc++ are both Itanium; libc++ only adds the __1 inline namespace to the chain). Gap{class_static_itanium_alias}: addVariable sets storage_alias_name for NAMESPACE-scope variables only (parser.cpp:18587,18601) via namespace_cpp_variable_symbol -> itanium_mangle_nested_var(qualifiers, name), and THAT MANGLER ALREADY TAKES AN ARBITRARY QUALIFIER CHAIN — a class name is one more qualifier than a namespace, so _ZNSt6locale7_S_onceE is within reach of existing machinery. Wire it at the class-static declaration and DELETE guard 2. Harder subset: template-class statics (basic_string<...>::npos) whose qualifier is a TEMPLATE-ID, needing template-argument mangling; excluded today by guard 1. VERIFY before promising — I have been over-pessimistic in this direction twice today.

FIX 2 @6fec105d — a nested type is a member of its enclosing scope, `struct` included. Two halves: the nested-STRUCT path never registered the scope entry the nested-CLASS path did (set_class_type_alias), and a `struct` was never a `::` scope at all. The second is fixed on the principle the promotion site ALREADY STATES: "The keyword does not decide struct-vs-class; the CONTENTS do." An object member and an NSDMI already earned class-hood; a nested type — which is what makes an aggregate a scope — now does too. A struct with no nested type is untouched, so trivial C structs stay DataDefSTRUCT and the zero-cost property that criterion protects is intact.

STILL OPEN — Gap{nested_tag_not_scoped_to_struct_body}: two scopes each declaring `struct Inner` collide ("Class 'Inner' already defined"), because a nested tag in a STRUCT body registers under its bare name at file scope. PLAN IS WORKED OUT (owner asked): valid C CANNOT produce this collision (in C a nested tagged struct has file scope, so two of them is a redefinition error there too) — so NO --std= gate is needed, which is what makes it small. parser.cpp:31285 ALREADY qualifies a nested tag's store key to `Outer::Inner` and renames the emitted identity to `Outer__Inner`; it just requires class_scope_stack non-empty, and only TokenCLASS::parse pushes that. Generalize that existing disambiguation to struct-body nesting. Resolution of Outer::Inner needs nothing new — the type_alias from fix 2 already does it. Check first whether the bare registration is visible as a TYPE at all (r41 says madc already rejects unqualified `Inner i;`, matching g++), because if it only serves the elaborated `struct Inner i;` the rule can be "always qualify" instead of "qualify on collision".

VLA NOT DEALLOCATED ON BACKWARD GOTO: a `goto` jumping back to before a VLA's declaration must deallocate the VLA (gcc/C semantics; gcc-torture 20040811-1.c). madc lowers VLAs as malloc + __attribute__((cleanup)), which frees only on SCOPE EXIT, not on the backward goto re-entering the scope — so a backward-goto loop over a VLA LEAKS one allocation per iteration. 20040811-1.c leaks ~2GB over 1e6 iterations; it passes only when memory is available (it OOM-SIGSEGV'd when the MIR fork's 128MB code-holder reservation reduced headroom — see mir_fork; arch-gated off x86-64, so it passes again).
